title: Reverse planner cost direction: raise random_page_cost 1.5->2.5, seq_page_cost 0.8->1.0
configuration_cause: Incumbent sits at random_page_cost=1.5 and seq_page_cost=0.8, both below the PostgreSQL defaults (4.0/1.0). r007 pushed them further down (1.1/0.7) and was refuted on TPS in 2 of 3 blocks; the cache-consistent low-cost direction is falsified, so the cost model is over-favoring random index paths relative to the actual cached regime.
mechanism: GetUserTweets consumes 88% of finite terminal capacity at p50=175us with an Index Scan plan. r007's downward cost move (1.5->1.1, 0.8->0.7) was refuted: TPS fell in blocks 2 and 3. Since reject_harmful is the only falsifying verdict and r007 was inconclusive-but-refuted on the TPS edge, reverse the group direction with equal-or-larger amplitude: raise random_page_cost to 2.5 and seq_page_cost to 1.0. This makes the planner less eager to choose random index paths for the dominant GetUserTweets template, favoring cheaper sequential/bitmap paths and reducing per-call page touches that occupy terminal time.
query_effect: Planner cost recalibration upward should keep GetUserTweets on a stable, cheaper access path and reduce per-call page touches; plan_evidence currently shows a single Index Scan at cost 8.45.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful transaction TPS if the reversed cost direction reduces GetUserTweets terminal occupancy; bounded because the dominant cost is client-side terminal saturation, not planner choice alone.
expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 and p95 should decrease slightly; overall p95 may be unchanged since it is dominated by the same template.

predictions.rationale: Reversed cost direction should reduce per-call page touches for the dominant template.
Tail of the dominant template should follow the p50 improvement if the access path is cheaper.
Freed terminal capacity from the dominant template raises completed-transaction TPS.

alternatives.statement: If the reversed cost direction does not change the GetUserTweets access path, TPS and p50 will be unchanged and the planner is not the bottleneck; the terminal saturation is purely client-side.

If WAL sync latency (0.137ms average, wal_wait anomaly) dominates InsertTweet and indirectly terminal time, TPS will not move with planner costs and the WAL commit-path bundle is the correct next action.

why_exceeds_incumbent: r007 tested the downward cost direction and was refuted on TPS; reversing with larger amplitude (random_page_cost 1.5->2.5, seq_page_cost 0.8->1.0) tests the opposite, untested direction of the same planner mechanism against the incumbent.

nodes.label: Reversed cost model favors cheaper access paths for GetUserTweets

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Reverse of refuted r007 direction (1.5->1.1); 2.5 is between incumbent 1.5 and default 4.0, within safe [1.0,6.0].
knob_changes.mechanism_role: planner cost of random/cached reads; raising it discourages random index paths

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Reverse of refuted r007 direction (0.8->0.7); 1.0 is the PostgreSQL default, within safe [0.5,2.0].
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost; raising it rebalances toward sequential paths
